why: The thirteen names, their schema lines, the exact text of the concurrent file and the edits to the generated file are all given and hold against the code, and the new catalog test, migration-safety.scan and db:check catch most slips. But it is a migration on orders, order_lines and visits that CI applies to production: dropping the wrong statement from the generated file, leaving a hot-table drop in the transactional file, or touching a similarly named index passes the tests, and the plan checks are by hand.
harm_if_wrong: A non-concurrent DROP INDEX that locks orders in production during the release, or a dropped index that was the only fast path for a read, slowing checkout or the orders list.
